intervals.label: installation and engineering runs
intervals.locator: HPS experiment page, "About the HPS Experiment"; installation: "installed at JLAB in February 2015"
intervals.note: Installed February 2015 (SLAC HPS page); the 2018 paper says installed and commissioned "early in the spring of 2015". Engineering runs: March-April 2015 and May 2016 (a 2016 run is the subject of arXiv:2212.10629).
intervals.quote: Engineering runs during March and April 2015 and May 2016 demonstrated that the experiment worked and produced physics quality data.

intervals.label: JLab approval of 165 days of running
intervals.locator: HPS experiment page, "About the HPS Experiment"
intervals.note: The page is undated prose written around early 2018 (it says the first HPS physics publication "will be submitted in Spring, 2018"); the approval date itself is not stated, so the year is approximate and the end (before the first protracted run, scheduled for summer 2019) is a bound.
intervals.quote: On the basis of these early results, JLAB has approved 165 days of running for the experiment.

intervals.note: Year precision. The May 2024 update says 30 of the remaining 135 PAC days had been used for the second physics run and the collaboration was preparing detector repairs for further operations; no source after May 2024 was found, so "active" is the latest documented state.
intervals.quote: HPS has taken high-luminosity data runs in 2019 and 2021 that will explore new dark photon phase space.

physics_goals.quote: The Heavy Photon Search (HPS) experiment in Hall-B at Jefferson Lab searches for heavy or dark photons that mix with ordinary photons through kinetic mixing
physics_goals.value: Search for heavy (dark) photons that mix with ordinary photons through kinetic mixing, using resonance and displaced-vertex signatures

summary.plain: HPS fires electrons from Jefferson Lab onto a thin tungsten foil and looks for electron-positron pairs that would reveal a hypothetical 'dark photon' - a new light force carrier tied to dark matter - either as a narrow bump in mass or as a pair born a little downstream of the target.
summary.technical: Fixed-target dark-photon search in the Hall B alcove: tungsten foil target, silicon micro-strip vertex tracker in a dipole magnet, PbWO4 calorimeter and scintillator hodoscope, searching for A' to e+e- resonances (20-220 MeV) and displaced vertices; engineering runs 2015-2016 (first limits at eps^2 ~ 10^-5), high-luminosity runs in 2019 and 2021, second physics run under way as of 2024.

unique_capabilities.quote: using a compact, large-acceptance forward spectrometer consisting of a tungsten foil target, a silicon micro-strip vertex tracker (SVT), a PbWO4 electromagnetic calorimeter (ECal), and a scintillation hodoscope (SH)
unique_capabilities.value: Compact large-acceptance forward spectrometer with a silicon vertex tracker placed millimetres from the beam, sensitive to both prompt resonances and displaced decay vertices
